texts: kabir style doha about a blind man doing all the rituals but seeing nothing inside
blind man, empty rituals
Write me a couplet on how a blind man can walk to every pilgrimage site and repeat every mantra, yet his heart stays shut, the ritual goes on and nothing real is ever touched.
my blind uncle never misses the pilgrimage bus and mutters prayers all day, then screams at the cook. a verse for him please
Like a sightless man circling holy places, he chants by rote while the light of truth never finds his eyes
pilgrimage without sincerity
doha on people who do puja every morning but cheat in business all day
Sacred journeys, hollow mantras, a spirit that bows to nothing: sing of the pilgrim whose feet roam far while his heart never leaves its place.
Our neighbour does a two hour puja daily and then shouts at his mother in law. Need a couplet that fits him.
I want a long doha about all the chanting sessions, holy visits and festival rounds people make to feel pious while their hearts stay cold, selfish and totally unchanged underneath all of it.
Kashi trips, mantra rounds
The hymn leaves the lips but never sinks into the heart; the rite is flawless and the soul stays untouched.
My cousin booked a fancy pilgrimage tour, posted forty photos, and hasn't called his sick father once. Give me a doha about that.
hey can u write something about people who do every ritual by the book and still stay mean
Please compose a long verse about the man who repeats the holy name a thousand times aloud, visits every sacred town, yet carries envy and greed in his chest exactly as before.
Write a verse on a king in his palace who pays for chanting day and night, while a chakor bird in the garden watches real devotion pass by unnoticed.
hey, a palace full of chanting while the heart stays empty, even the chakor bird sees through it, make it a doha
palace, chakor bird, fake worship
The chakor bird yearns for light alone, yet palace dwellers bow with cold lips and never taste the nectar of true love
The big boss in our city held a grand yagna at his palace while a chakor bird called outside and his workers waited unpaid. A verse for that evening please.
Within this house the holy pictures glitter and hymns ring out, yet no one has bowed in truth; pour that sorrow into two lines.
Write a doha about a house with a whole shelf of rituals, where aunty keeps a schedule for every mantra but has not forgiven her own sister for twelve long years.
house full of puja
We hold a big prayer ceremony in the house every month, with chanting and incense, but my brother and I are not speaking. Something meaningful for this please?
a doha for my house where everyone does morning prayers loudly but nobody listens to each other
A verse for the man who rises before dawn to recite his prayers for hours, then shortchanges every worker, snaps at his family, and calls it all a holy routine that keeps him pure.
mantras, no mercy
my boss touches the feet of every holy man who visits the office but docks salary for a single minute of lateness, ugh
Lips that murmur the holy name, a heart that keeps its cruelty folded away.
write a doha, people who chant a lot but never change
door, grindstone, hollow prayer
A verse about the man who opens his door each morning to a long routine of bowing and chanting, and yet his heart turns like a grindstone, grinding people down all day long.
doha about the daily puja grind, same door same chants every day, and the grindstone of the mind never stops
Ravi's mom does puja at the door every dawn and then runs the maid down like a grindstone all day. I want a couplet for her.
At the door the prayers are laid down like flowers, but the grindstone of the heart still crushes everything that comes near
The physician of the soul is not found in the priest's loud chant; the rite is recited, the sickness stays.
The village priest asked us for a big payment for a special rite, and my father's physician said the real trouble was loneliness, not bad omens. Give us a doha about this.
Compose a couplet for the priest who collects fees for elaborate rituals promising a cure, while the physician quietly sees that no empty chant ever healed a troubled mind.
physician, priest, empty rites
yo doha about a priest selling ritual fixes and a physician who knows it doesn't work
My grandmother keeps winding a sacred thread around the same holy post every year, saying the knot saves the family, but she still carries grudges. Need a doha about this.
Make me a doha about all the ritual knots people tie, tying a thread on the wrist or on a post, believing it guards them, while the mind itself stays tangled in desire and pride.
Tied thread upon thread, vow upon vow, yet the knot in the heart is never loosened.
ritual thread tying thing, people think it works lol, write a doha
sacred thread, hollow ritual
Pilgrim's feet blister on the long road to the holy city, but the heart stayed back at the counter counting coins.
doha pls, someone did the whole char dham tour and came back just as rude as before
I need a doha about a man who spends his savings on a grand pilgrimage and chants at every halt, yet returns as greedy and short tempered as the day he left his village.
tour holy places, remain unchanged
Papa came back from the long pilgrimage with a hundred photos and the same temper. Mom just sighed. Could you put that sigh into a doha?
yaar write something on people who make their prayers into a performance but their hearts stay cold
Fragrant smoke, ringing hymns, a thousand bowed heads, and not one soul awake
Last week the whole colony gathered for a night long jagran and next morning the same people were fighting about parking. Doha please?
Give me two lines on the festival crowd that sings and bows for hours, shares sweets, and takes photographs, though not one of them has asked what the prayers were truly meant to change in the heart.
rituals without a changed heart
The cleric near our lane loudly leads rituals at the door of every wedding but takes a cut from the poor family's savings. What would Kabir say?
door, cleric, empty ritual
The cleric guards the door of faith with a loud voice and open palm, while the One he names stays far outside.
A couplet please for the cleric who stands at the door performing rites for payment, telling everyone how to pray, while his own life is untouched by the very words he recites.
make a doha: the cleric at the door preaches rituals but doesn't live by them
A rich uncle at the wedding gave a sword donation and a gold donation to the pilgrimage fund so everyone would clap, yet his driver goes unpaid. Doha idea for that?
Gold offered, sword raised in a grand rite, and the Beloved smiles at none of it.
Compose a doha about the man who gifts gold and a ceremonial sword to a holy site with great ritual and publicity, believing it buys favour, while his own conduct stays crooked and unkind.
gold, sword, hollow rites
doha about a gold and sword ceremony with fancy rituals but zero heart
Write about a blind man led by a lion of pride through the grand pilgrimage rounds, ringing out his chants, who thinks the ritual makes him holy while he cannot see his own fierce arrogance.
blind man + lion + empty rituals, make me a doha
blind man, lion, pilgrimage
My boss walks around like a lion after his daily prayers, and he is totally like a blind man to how his staff feel. Can you turn that into a doha?
The blind man follows the roar of the lion and calls the noise worship.
doha about someone who prays a ton but never helps anyone
The lips repeat the holy name; the hands remain closed.
Compose two lines about empty devotion: a person who attends every prayer gathering and every fast day pilgrimage, yet turns away the needy and treats the truth as an unwelcome guest.
Every festival our relative donates for the big prayer function, then pretends not to know us when mom needs help with hospital bills. Doha for that please
prayer without kindness
rituals, rounds, nothing inside
What is the use of walking the sacred path when the walker has not moved an inch within?
my friend does every holy tour and ritual she can find but cries that she still feels empty and angry. I told her Kabir might have an answer
Share a doha about how a person may travel to every pilgrimage site, perform each prescribed rite, and chant until dawn, but finds no peace, because sincerity was left behind at home.
write a doha about doing rituals mechanically without feeling it
Grandpa taught the family parrot to say the holy names and everyone claimed it was a blessing, but a pearl necklace for puja mattered more to him than the words. Doha please?
Pen a doha about a parrot taught to repeat a holy phrase and a pearl worn for sacred ceremonies: both gleam and recite, but neither knows the meaning, like the ritual crowd.
The parrot repeats the sacred phrase like a pearl strung on a string of habit, lovely and understood by none.
doha: parrot repeating mantras, pearl necklace for puja, all show no meaning
parrot, pearl, empty chants
Write a doha on the warrior who polishes his sword and recites prayers before every raid, feeling the ritual blesses his violence, though his heart remains as hard as the blade he carries.
my neighbour is a retired soldier who keeps his old sword on a puja altar and bows to it daily, yet he beats his dog. thoughts, kabir?
sword, ritual, hard heart
a doha about people praying over a sword before doing harm, hollow rituals
Sword blessed with flowers and chants, still hungry for blood; what prayer is this?
pls write a doha about people who recite scriptures from memory but never apply any of it
scripture reciters, unchanged hearts
My teacher can recite whole verses by heart at every ceremony but gossips about every student behind their back. A line for her?
Compose a doha about the scholar who knows every verse for every ceremony and is invited to recite at each gathering, but whose mind is full of envy and whose life never matches his words.
Memorized verses spill from his mouth like water from a cracked vessel, and nothing remains.
Write a couplet about a pilgrim who bathes and chants at every holy place on his long journey while a fish in the water below stays faithful to its home all its life and needs no pilgrimage.
The fish lives in the water always, yet man travels far to find what was never lost.
doha about how a fish lives in water all its life but humans go to far holy places to find purity
fish, pilgrimage, empty rites
Our family spent a lot to go on a pilgrimage while my brother, who feeds the fish in our village tank every day, is the only one who actually seems at peace. A doha for him?
doha: winnowing fan thing, peacock dancing, puja without meaning
winnowing fan, peacock, hollow puja
The peacock spreads its plumes before the crowd; take the winnowing fan to the rite and see how little grain is left.
Compose a doha in which the peacock displays its fine feathers for the ritual audience, and the winnowing fan sifts out the husk, as Kabir might sift real devotion from the empty show of ceremony.

At my sister's wedding the puja was so elaborate, peacock feathers everywhere, and when the winnowing fan of time passed over it all, only a few honest hearts were left. Could you write something like that?
my mother in law sits with her prayer beads at every family gathering, lips moving, eyes watching who gets which dish. need a doha
prayer beads, no sincerity
A doha about the person who rolls prayer beads between the fingers all day long while the mind wanders to money, gossip and revenge, and nothing within is changed by all that counting.
write a doha: prayer beads in hand but mind somewhere else entirely
The prayer beads turn in the hand, the mind turns in the marketplace of desire.
one-string lute, sandalwood, show
the singer at our satsang plays his one-string lute beautifully and wears sandalwood paste but is rude to the volunteers. line for him?
Sandalwood on the brow, the one-string lute in hand, a hymn on his lips and none in his heart
doha about fancy sandalwood and one-string lute kind of religious people who are rude off stage
Write a doha about the devotional singer with a one-string lute and a smear of sandalwood paste who is celebrated at every gathering, yet whose private life is bitter and far from the songs he sings.
hey doha pls: the oil press keeps turning, the cloth sheet is for puja only, ritual without understanding
Our family runs an oil press and every Friday we spread a clean cloth sheet for the special puja, but dad still short weights the customers. Could you put that in a verse?

Write about the oil press running day after day, squeezing the poor, and the owner who spreads a fresh cloth sheet before his ritual prayers each morning, believing the ceremony washes away his unfair profits.
oil press, cloth sheet, rituals
The oil press grinds out its bitter share while a spotless cloth sheet is laid for prayer.
potter and clay, hollow worship
Our local potter says people bring him clay wares for their rituals but never ask him about his life; he makes them with love, they buy them with habit. Doha for him?

Compose a doha about how the potter shapes clay with his own hands, while men perform elaborate worship around the shaped vessel, forgetting that the Maker lives in patient work and sincere living, not in noise.
doha about the potter and clay vs people doing rituals with no heart
The potter works the clay in silence and love, yet the crowd's fancy rituals do not know his name.
My grandmother, after attending the cremation rites of her neighbour, held a mirror to her own face and wondered if the bier prayers she had done meant anything. Kabir doha?
Write a couplet about the mirror of the soul and the bier of death: people carry out the full ritual for the dead, yet never gaze into the mirror to see their own heart.
doha: mirror, bier, empty rituals at funerals nobody feels
Beside the bier they chant, before the mirror they preen: the ritual is everywhere, the self is nowhere.
mirror, bier, hollow rites
Last Diwali my uncle spent a fortune on the ceremony and invited everyone, but on the same day refused to pay his servant's medical bill. what a hypocrite
An altar of flowers by day, a heart of briars by night; how long will this ritual fool the One who sees?

I want a Kabir style doha on how some people perform every holy ritual with great care and noise, believing that the ritual alone earns merit, while their daily dealings with others remain unkind and dishonest.
write about people doing puja for appearance sake but behaving badly
puja without honesty
doha about the bell thing, people ring it hard at the holy place and think God listens only then
The bell rings out over the heads of the crowd, but the silence of the heart is what He hears.
A doha on the one who rings the bell loudly at every prayer and thinks the noise reaches heaven, though the stillness of an honest mind would be heard without any ringing at all.
bell, ritual, noise
My cousin rings the bell at the holy place so loudly every morning that the neighbours complain, and then he ignores his own mother calling from the kitchen. Make it a doha?
My dad does the long morning rituals in perfect order but forgets to ask how I am doing. I wish I could tell him something with a verse
He counts every rite like a miser counts coins, and love goes unspent.
Make a doha for a person who has memorized every step of every rite and never skips a single chant, yet finds himself spiritually empty because the steps were never meant to be a substitute for love.
doha idea: so many people follow ritual rules strictly but have zero compassion
rites without love
weaver's loom, pilgrimage, hollow
The old weaver at our lane works at his loom all day and says that is his prayer, while his rich neighbours go on pilgrimage trips and come back restless. Could you write a doha for him?
At the weaver's loom the weaver is at prayer, while the pilgrim wanders far from his own quiet center.
Write a doha comparing the weaver at his loom, honest in his daily work and at peace, with the pilgrims who travel far, perform every rite, and return with the same restless hearts they left with.
doha: the weaver's loom keeps working while people run to far pilgrimages for peace
my aunt wears expensive musk perfume to every holy event and hunts for peace like a musk deer in the wrong place, with a snake of ego curled inside her. Kabir would have words for her
snake, musk deer, empty rituals
Write a doha about the musk deer wandering the wilds searching for the scent that is in its own body, just like people chasing pilgrimage and ritual to find what a snake of ego keeps hidden within.
The musk deer searches the wilds for the fragrance in its navel, while man circles holy places with a snake of pride coiled in his heart.
doha with snake and musk deer about people doing rituals to find what's already inside them
doha about people who do puja for show but cheat their neighbours
The altar glows with offered light, the hand beneath it reaches into another's pocket.
The man who runs the local ceremony committee was caught short-changing the flower sellers last week. People still bow to him at every function. What a doha that would make.
ritual cheat

Write two lines on the one who leads every public ritual with great flourish and devotion, draws crowds and praise, but weighs his daily dealings with greed and tells small lies whenever he sees a gain.
fasting, chanting, going nowhere
doha about rituals with no inner change lol
I went to see my school friend after twenty years. He has become a very devout man who chants all day, but he is still the same bully, only now with scripture quotes.
Write a doha for the follower who adds rite after rite to his day and calls it progress, though not one of them has loosened his pride or taught him gentleness toward the people living around him.
Rite upon rite is piled like bricks, yet the builder has not left the ground.
doha: an arrow flying, a pilgrimage that never hits the target, empty prayers
arrow, pilgrimage, empty chanting
A flying arrow of prayer that never leaves the bow of the lips falls short of the mark.
Compose a doha about the arrow of devotion that must pierce the heart to reach its mark, while the pilgrim's ritual shots all fall short, aimed at holy places and not at his own inner truth.
My uncle took up archery and says it is his yoga, while his pilgrimage trips every year bring back nothing. He once told me the arrow knows more truth than the tours. Can you write a doha on that?
After my father died, relatives came to do all the rites in a hurry, checked the clock, and left before the meal. Nobody cried. Could you write a doha for that sadness?
Please write a couplet about those who perform the prescribed rites in a rush, glance at the time, and leave as soon as the final chant is done, the ritual completed on paper but never in the heart.
write doha on rushed rituals, ticking the box kind of worship
ritual as checklist
The rite is done, the guests depart, and not one tear has fallen to water the soil of the heart.
Healer of bodies, reader of scripts, the physician and the reciter both stand at the sickbed while the sickness is in the pride; neither rite nor herb has reached it.
Write a doha about the physician who prescribes strange rituals along with his medicine and takes money for both, though the real cure for a restless mind is honesty and not a single borrowed chant.
physician, empty ritual
doha pls: physician selling puja packages with treatment, kabir would roast him
When my mother was ill, the doctor suggested we also hire a puja for her recovery. We paid twice, and what she really needed was her family beside her. Doha for that?
He counts holy names the way a clerk counts coins, and the Name does not live in the count.
doha idea: counting mantras 108 times but missing the point of the mantra
counting mantras, missing meaning
Compose a verse about the devotee who sets a daily target of a thousand chants and celebrates when he completes it, though the sound of the name has never softened his heart or his speech.
my roommate keeps a notebook of how many times he chanted today and gets upset if he misses the number, but he never washes his own dishes. doha?
doha: fish in a pond, sword in a ritual, fake spirituality, you get it
Our family reciter wanted us to put a fish in a bowl and bless a sword for luck, charging a fortune. Mom just shook her head. A doha to say what she thought?
Please compose a doha on the man of rites who chants over a fish in the water and a sword in the hand, selling protection to the anxious, while the true protector sits in the heart unsought.
Over the fish and the sword the rite is recited, yet the true shield is hidden in a quiet heart.
fish, sword, empty rites

A doha about the oil press that squeezes the poor, and the owner who performs great rituals each morning and pours offerings, hoping the ceremony will cover the pressure he puts on his workers every single day.
The oil press turns all day, squeezing; at dawn the owner pours his ritual offering to wash the stain.
oil press, hollow ritual
doha: the oil press owner does a puja every day but underpays workers
Where I work, the boss does a long ceremony every morning before opening the oil press and then sacks people without notice. Please give me a doha for it
write a doha about a leaf offered in puja but the heart left out
My neighbour gets up at four to pick leaves and flowers for her ritual offerings, then spends the evening saying nasty things about everyone on the street. doha?
One green leaf is offered at the altar, but the heart that should be offered is still withheld.
leaf, offering, no devotion

Compose a doha on those who gather leaves and flowers for their ceremonies, arrange them just so, and think the offering has been made, while the one real offering, the surrender of ego, is never given.
seed, pot of water, ritual
doha: pouring water from a pot on a seed won't make it sprout if the soil of the heart is dead, ritual pointless

Write a verse about the man who pours the pot of water over the seed with elaborate ritual and speeches, hoping for a harvest, while the soil of his own mind is hardened and nothing sincere is planted.
The pot of water is poured, the seed is sown with a chant, but the ground of the heart remains dry and hard.
My father in law performed a seed sowing ceremony with a big pot of water and a hired reciter, yet cut down the village's old fields next day. I wish Kabir could comment
doha on the neighbour who attends every holy event and still hates his brother
For three years my uncle has done every fast and pilgrimage on the calendar. Last month he still would not attend his brother's daughter's wedding. A couplet for him?
devout in public only
Write a doha about the believer who joins every ritual gathering, wears the right look, and speaks the right words, yet nurses an old hatred for his own brother that no ceremony has ever touched.
Many altars he has bowed at, but one room in his own heart he has locked for years.
Write a doha about a yogi who has set up a big oil press of ceremonies, pressing out fees and offerings from followers each morning, while his own mind remains unchanged by all that grand ritual.
doha pls, yogi plus oil press metaphor for money hungry rituals
yogi, oil press, hollow rites
The yogi who came to our colony set up an elaborate ritual hall like an oil press for donations and demanded ghee, and by the end of the month he had a new car. What would Kabir say?
The yogi turns the oil press of ritual, and the people provide the oil, while the Truth he speaks of slips by.

Compose a doha about those who observe a fixed calendar of rituals, from sunrise rites to evening chants, believing that routine alone makes them holy, though not one of those rites has ever made them kinder or humbler.
My grandma follows her ritual calendar like a train schedule, never missing a single rite, but she is quite cold toward the new bahu. Could we capture that in a doha?
By the calendar they pray, by the calendar they weep, and the heart has no hour of its own.
doha about people following rituals like a rulebook
ritual calendar, cold hearts
doha: forehead mark, rainbird calling, ritual people who don't actually yearn
The rainbird calls for the true drop alone, but the forehead mark bows to every passing shower of ceremony.
My grandfather is a man with a bright forehead mark who daily recites mantras, but unlike the rainbird he never yearns for anything beyond habit. What would you write about him?
forehead mark, rainbird, no longing

Write a verse where the rainbird cries for one pure raindrop with real longing, in contrast to the person with a fancy forehead mark who attends every ritual and yearns for nothing deeper than applause.

A doha about the one who counts prayer beads from morning to night, murmuring the holy name with lips alone, while the mind runs after property and quarrels, and no devotion actually ties the heart to anything divine.
Prayer beads slide through the fingers, as years slide through the days, and the mind never once turns inward.
prayer beads, false devotion
In the bus, a lady next to me kept moving her prayer beads, but she was shouting at the conductor and cursing the driver. What a scene! Kabir doha?
doha about prayer beads and fake devotion pls
The snake sheds its skin and thinks the shedding is holiness; the poison stays in the fang.
The man who leads our weekly ritual is gentle in the hall but a snake in business, we all know it. A doha for what we all see?
snake, ritual, hidden poison
doha: snake in the grass as a ritual leader, you know the type
Write a doha about the person who changes his outer rites and clothing every season, much like a snake that sheds its skin, while the venom of cruelty and greed within remains the same.
After a huge pilgrimage trip with the whole extended family, we came home and the arguments about land started again the very same evening. Is there a doha for that?
holy trip, same quarrels

I'd like a doha about the family that takes the grandest pilgrimage together, bathes, bows, and chants in every place, and then returns to petty fights over land and money, exactly as if the journey had never happened.
Back from the sacred road with dust on the feet and old quarrels in the heart.
write something on rituals not changing the person who does them
doha: thorn in the heart even after sandalwood and rituals, pls
A friend of mine wears fragrant sandalwood to every ceremony, and still pricks everyone with sharp comments like a thorn. Could you write a verse about her?
Sandalwood cools the brow, but the thorn remains in the speech.
sandalwood, thorn, hollow ritual

Compose a Kabir style doha on the ritual devotee who applies cooling sandalwood paste and looks serene, but whose words are thorns that wound anyone who comes near, and who sees no contradiction in this.
A verse for the regular who is first in the queue at every ceremony and last to forgive anyone, who drops coins in the box with great show yet will not spare a kind word for a struggling neighbour.
Every morning my father in law stands at the front of the prayer line, and every evening he turns the neighbours' children away. A doha please
first in line, unforgiving
doha about people who show up to every ritual and are still unkind
First at the altar, last to the open hand of mercy.
